messages:
maya: quick q — can we do pseudonymization instead of redaction for inspect-mode telemetry? preserves token/structure for evals but reduces PII.

ron: interesting. do we mean reversible pseudonymization or deterministic hash? compliance will care.

nik: deterministic HMAC per-tenant salt is my vote — unlinkable across tenants. no reversible keys stored in app.

emily: :thinking_face: keep in mind console UX — consistent pseudonyms can still deanonymize when combined with other attrs.

sre-anna: from oncall perspective, will this hamper debugging? we sometimes need to contact users; need breakglass with audit trail.

nik: breakglass possible via KMS-wrapped one-time unwrap token; require 2-person approval and audit log entry.

maya: proposal: two-tier telemetry
- 100% metadata (pseudonymized)
- 1% full payloads stored encrypted in secure vault for quality/regression evals

maya: sample config snippet:
```
telemetry.pseudonymize = {
  method: "HMAC-SHA256",
  salt_source: "route_salt",
  output: "hex",
  keep_structure: true
}
```

ron: how is this surfaced in console? per-route toggle or global? canary rollout?

maya: per-route toggle + org-level override. canary with 10% of traffic -> 3-day window, failback to redaction.

console-bot: deploy triggered: telemetry-service/v3 canary -> 2026-04-02T11:05Z

emily: legal ok? will confirm but prefer non-reversible approach and clear labeling in UI.

nik: quick perf note: HMAC at ingest adds ~0.3ms per request on avg, batching helps.

sre-anna: also add metric: 'inspect_unmasked_requests.count' gated by breakglass, plus alert if >0 outside approved window.

ron: also need quota implications; storing pseudonymized metadata should be cheap but 1% full payloads -> storage cost bump. link to cost model?

maya: agree. action items:
- nik: prototype pseudonymizer + canary (this week)
- emily: legal check + wording for console label
- anna: runbook for breakglass and alerting
- maya: console wireframes for per-route toggle and canary UI

ron: :thumbsup: any objections? if none i'll add to roadmap and schedule design review.

emily: :+1:

nik: will open PR with PoC and perf numbers.

sre-anna: adding runbook draft to /docs/oncall/inspect-breakglass.md

maya: thanks everyone — we'll sync in standup tomorrow.
